title: Discretisation schemes
_comment: Only the per-group `default` entries are form-editable, and that is the
honest boundary rather than a shortcut.
A group's other entries name the operand in the key itself —
`div(phi,U)`, `grad(p)` — so the set of keys depends on the equations the
case solves and cannot be enumerated in advance. `divSchemes/default` is
`none` in 16 of the 23 corpus cases precisely because those cases specify
every divergence term explicitly. Those entries are preserved untouched and
edited in the text tab (§5.4, FR-P6).
Values are free text, not enums. A scheme is a phrase whose tail can name
an operand — `bounded Gauss linearUpwind grad(U)` — so the set is open. A
dropdown here would be a list that is wrong for every interesting case.

fields.label: Time derivative
fields.help: steadyState for a steady run; Euler or backward for a transient one.

fields.label: Gradient
fields.help: Usually 'Gauss linear'. 'cellLimited' variants help on poor meshes.

fields.label: Divergence
fields.help: Often 'none', which requires every divergence term to be named explicitly below it in the text tab.

fields.label: Laplacian
fields.help: 'Gauss linear corrected' is the usual choice; the last word is the non-orthogonal correction.

fields.label: Surface-normal gradient
fields.help: 'corrected' on a non-orthogonal mesh, 'orthogonal' only when the mesh truly is.

fields.label: Wall-distance method
fields.help: Needed by turbulence models that use distance to the wall.
